title: Fix misleading edge overlap in routing
author: tegonzalez
body:
This change fixes a routing failure in diagrams where an outgoing branch could visually reuse the approach corridor of an unrelated incoming edge, changing the apparent meaning of the diagram.

The concrete failure case was:

```
  graph LR
  A --> C
  B --> C
  C --> D
  C --> E
```

- Before this change, the C -> E branch could overlap the B -> C approach into C, which made the output read as though the branch split from the B -> C path instead of from C.
- To address that, I updated edge routing to treat previously routed edge cells as soft occupancy during path selection. Overlap with unrelated edges now carries a penalty, while overlap within the same fan-in or fan-out family remains allowed so intentional shared trunks still render cleanly. I also fixed occupancy tracking so merged path segments are expanded back into unit grid cells correctly.
- Unicode golden test for the discovered case `bun test src/__tests__/ascii.test.ts src/__tests__/ascii-multiline.test.ts`

title: fix: add iteration limit to A* pathfinder to prevent OOM on dense graphs
author: ktrysmt
body:
## Summary

- `getPath()` in `src/ascii/pathfinder.ts` had no upper bound on A* iterations. On dense TD flowcharts with multiple fan-in edge bundles, the destination could become unreachable through free grid cells, causing the search to expand indefinitely until hitting V8's Map size limit (~16.7M entries) and throwing `RangeError: Map maximum size exceeded`.
- Added a `MAX_ITERATIONS` (50,000) guard that returns `null` when exceeded. The callers (`routeBundledEdges`) already handle `null` gracefully by falling back to straight-line segments.
- Added `pathfinder.test.ts` covering `getPath`, `heuristic`, `mergePath`, and a regression test for the dense-graph crash.

title: fix: use edge-target check for root detection instead of order-dependent scan
author: ktrysmt
body:
## Summary

- The root detection in `createMapping` (`src/ascii/grid.ts`) used a forward scan over `graph.nodes` in parser insertion order. When `child -> parent` edges were defined after `parent -> grandchild` edges, the parent node was misclassified as a root, causing fan-in groups to be placed on the same level as their children (flat horizontal layout instead of a tree).
- Replaced with a direct edge-target check: nodes that are never the target of any edge are roots. When all nodes are edge targets (pure cycles or self-references), falls back to the original forward-scan heuristic to preserve definition-order semantics.
- Updated `preserve_order_of_definition` golden test to reflect the corrected layout where B (the only in-degree 0 node) is correctly placed as the root.

Fixes #65

## Test plan

- [x] `bun test src/__tests__/` — all 711 tests pass, no regressions
- [x] Verified cycle cases (`back_reference_from_child`, `self_reference`, `self_reference_with_edge`) still pass via the fallback path
- [x] Verified the dense fan-in diagram from #64 now produces a proper hierarchical layout

title: fix: group root nodes by downstream target and align fan-in children
author: ktrysmt
body:
## Summary

- Root nodes feeding into different targets were placed in a flat horizontal sequence, causing edge paths from different fan-in groups to overlap and become unreadable.
- Group roots by their immediate downstream target so roots for the same target are placed contiguously.
- When placing fan-in targets (in-degree > 1), align them with the parent's perpendicular position using `Math.max(levelTracker, parentPerpendicular)` to keep targets near their root group.

For `A1, A2 --> A` and `B1, B2 --> B`:

```
A1   A2   B1   B2

      |    |
      A    B
```

**After:** roots grouped by target, targets aligned under their groups
```
A1   A2        B1   B2
 └────┘         └────┘
      |              |
      A              B
```

title: Fix nested-subgraph layout when direction is set
author: ayrtonmassey
body:
Issue
=====

Mermaid source can declare a `direction` directive on each subgraph and connect any leaf to any other leaf. beautiful-mermaid honoured neither when subgraphs were nested:

- **Per-subgraph `direction` was ignored.** Nested `direction LR` inside a `TD` parent silently laid out top-to-bottom anyway.
- **Cross-subgraph edges broke under `SEPARATE_CHILDREN`.** ELK can only route an edge whose source and target are direct siblings, so an edge crossing a `SEPARATE_CHILDREN` boundary either failed to route or routed through subgraph headers and stair-stepped through tight gaps.

Cause
=====

ELK Layered offers two compound-graph modes:

- `INCLUDE_CHILDREN` flattens everything into one layered layout in the parent's direction. Cross-subgraph edges route fine, but per-subgraph `direction` directives are ignored.
- `SEPARATE_CHILDREN` lays out each subgraph independently in its own direction. But edges crossing a `SEPARATE_CHILDREN` boundary can't be drawn as a single polyline — ELK only routes an edge where source and target are direct siblings.

Combining "honour directions" with "allow cross-subgraph edges" needs work on top of ELK. The pre-fix code attempted `SEPARATE_CHILDREN` with two latent bugs that masked each other (`hierarchyHandling: 'SEPARATE'` is an invalid enum that ELK silently treats as default; ports had no `port.side`), so direction never took effect and ports collided.

Fix
===

Decompose every cross-subgraph edge into a chain of ELK *sub-edges*, one per subgraph boundary it crosses, joined at explicit boundary ports placed on the side dictated by each subgraph's effective direction. At the ELK level every edge is now internal — its source and target are direct siblings — so ELK routes the whole thing in one pass. After ELK runs, concatenate each chain's polylines back into the single user-visible edge.

Full algorithm — ten pipeline stages with input / output / failure-mode-without-it per stage — is the top-of-file docstring on `src/layout-engine/index.ts`.

Changes
=======

**Layout engine** (`src/layout-engine.ts` → `src/layout-engine/`)

- Split the 1,498-line monolith into a directory of pipeline-phase files: `index.ts` (public API + algorithm narrative), `preprocess-graph.ts` (stages 1–4), `elk-layout.ts` (stages 5–8), `postprocess-graph.ts` (stages 9–10), `utilities.ts` (phase-agnostic helpers + `pushTo`/`addTo` map-of-collection helpers).
- `computeSubgraphsNeedingSeparate` is now three independent subroutines unioned by an orchestrator — direction mismatch, leaf-endpoint containment, port passthrough — instead of a single function with a post-hoc mutation at the call site.
- `DEFAULTS.thoroughness: 30` (was `3`). Higher ELK cross-minimisation effort is required for the iterative barycentre pass (stage 8) to converge to zero-crossing layouts on dense fan-out/fan-in samples; verified by the `stress-dataflow-fan-out-fan-in` sample.
- Legacy trunk-bundling path removed (`mergeEdges`, the `elk.layered.highDegreeNodes.*` options). Port-chain routing supersedes it.

**Renaming pass**

- `cross-hier(archy)` → `cross-subgraph` everywhere — identifiers, comments, test names, slugs.
- `srcChain`/`tgtChain` → `sourceChain`/`targetChain`; `srcSg`/`tgtSg` → `sourceSubgraphId`/`targetSubgraphId`; `srcAnc`/`tgtAnc` → `sourceAncestor`/`targetAncestor`.
- `CrossHierDecomposition` → `PreprocessedEdge`, `CrossHierPort` → `CrossSubgraphPort`, `decompositions` → `preprocessedEdges`, `decompByIndex` → `preprocessedByEdgeIndex`, `decomp` → `preprocessed`.
- `countRightAngleCrossings` → `countPerpendicularCrossings`; `right-angle crossings` → `perpendicular crossings` in prose.
- `CROSSING_EPSILON`, `COORD_EPSILON`, and the inline `const EPS = 0.5` all collapse to a single shared `COORDINATE_EQUALITY_TOLERANCE`.

**Renderer** (`src/renderer.ts` + `src/render-geometry.ts`)

- `HOP_RADIUS`, `HOP_HEIGHT`, `HOP_ENDPOINT_PAD` (was an inline magic `6` in the engine), and `COORDINATE_EQUALITY_TOLERANCE` move into a shared `src/render-geometry.ts` module.
- `RenderOptions.renderHops?: boolean` (default `true`) added. The module-level `const RENDER_HOPS = true` toggle is gone; callers can now opt out per-render through the options object. A `%%{init:{hops:false}}%%` mermaid-source equivalent is left as a follow-up.

**Comments / docs**

- Every function in `src/layout-engine/**/*.ts` and `src/renderer.ts` now has a preceding `/** */` block that states what it is *for* (not the mechanics) and explains the failure mode it prevents where relevant.
- Phase section headers in `elk-layout.ts` and `preprocess-graph.ts` are 3–5 line blocks naming the phase, its input, and its output.
- `barycentre` is defined on first use; the LCA-cycle handler leads with the failure mode; the polyline simplifier explains the ELK output quirk it works around.

**Test coverage** (`src/__tests__/`)

- New `sample-graphs/separate-children-reason-2-leaf-migration.ts` and `separate-children-reason-3-port-passthrough.ts` — each isolates one of the previously-uncovered `SEPARATE_CHILDREN` reasons via `containment` and `expectedEdgesReachTargets` metadata.
- New inline property-test sections in `layout-properties.test.ts` for the same two reasons. Each asserts (a) the leaf stays inside its declared subgraph, (b) the cross-subgraph edge polyline reaches the target's bounding box, (c) layout is deterministic.
- Gallery flowcharts from `samples-data.ts` now wrap as `SampleGraph` entries at import time and join `ALL_SAMPLES` in the parameterised loop. The old hand-written `describe('published-gallery flowcharts')` block is gone; its leaf-inside-graph-rectangle assertion is promoted to a universal per-sample check.

**Comparison tooling** (`tools/sample-comparison/`)

- Dim-only diff metric replaced with a three-channel structural diff: outer dims, node-rect count + total area, edge `<path>` count + total polyline length + per-edge-id centroid drift (matched on `data-from`/`data-to`). DIFFERS gates on any channel > 1%; the badge surfaces all three so a reviewer can see which axis moved. mmc remains a reference column and is never part of the diff.
- Panel template extracted to a single shared `template-panel.html` with placeholders `{{HEADER_LABEL}}`, `{{HEADER_QUALIFIER}}`, `{{DIMS}}`, `{{SVG}}`, `{{DIFFERS_CLASS}}`. The row template now slots three uniform panels into `{{BEFORE_PANEL}}` / `{{AFTER_PANEL}}` / `{{MMC_PANEL}}`. `template-mmc-panel.html` deleted.

Testing
=======

- `bun test src/__tests__/layout-samples.test.ts src/__tests__/layout-properties.test.ts`: **414 pass / 0 fail** (up from 231 on the pre-fix baseline — gallery flowcharts now run through the parameterised loop, and two new sample files cover the previously-undocumented `SEPARATE_CHILDREN` reasons).
- The 100 failures in `src/__tests__/ascii.test.ts` and `ascii-edge-styles.test.ts` are pre-existing Unicode rendering issues on `main` and unrelated to this PR.
- Comparison-tool output (before/after SVGs + structural diff page) verified manually via `tools/sample-comparison/` — no regressions across the 100+ curated samples.

Reviewer Guidance
=================

- Start with the top-of-file docstring on `src/layout-engine/index.ts` — full algorithm narrative as ten numbered stages with input/output/failure-mode per stage.
- Each file under `src/layout-engine/` is one phase; the file docstring + section headers state what each function in the file is for.
- The 13 round-six remediation commits land in order from §14 (small reverts) through §15 (function-doc audit final pass). The commit boundaries are deliberately small so individual cleanups are easy to follow.

title: Fixes #111 Fixes #112
author: rmvegasm
body:
## Fix edge routing trunk sharing, box-start connector placement, and collinear corner detection

### Summary

Three bugs in the ASCII edge-routing pipeline that caused poor visual output for fan-out graphs (one source, multiple targets). The fixes span six files with coordinated changes to the A* pathfinder, drawing layer, and grid layout.

### Changes

#### 1. Deterministic A* tie-breaking + direction-ordered exploration

**Problem:** When two candidate paths have equal Manhattan cost, the `MinHeap`'s LIFO tie-breaking (`<` in `sinkDown`) picks paths non-deterministically. Additionally, old branch items from early A* expansion stay in the queue and get explored before more direct items from later expansion — creating "false detours."

**Fix (`pathfinder.ts`, `edge-routing.ts`):**
- `MinHeap.sinkDown`: `<` → `<=` gives FIFO ordering within each priority level; earlier-pushed nodes (more direct paths) are preferred
- `buildMoveDirs()`: orders MOVE_DIRS so the edge's initial cardinal direction is explored first (Right for TD Right-exit edges, Down for LR Down-exit edges)
- `getPath()` accepts optional `preferredDir` parameter
- `determinePath()` passes `preferredDir` to both preferred and alternative `getPath` calls

#### 2. Trunk-sharing post-processing

**Problem:** Sibling edges from the same source with the same start direction route independently and don't converge on a shared trunk segment. The Right edge detours to y=2 instead of sharing y=1 with Center (TD). The Bot edge detours to x=2 instead of sharing x=1 with Mid (LR).

**Fix (`grid.ts`, `types.ts`, `converter.ts`):**
- After initial edge routing, group edges by `(source, startDir)`
- For the second and subsequent edges in each group, re-route A* from the first edge's branch point (where it turns toward its target) instead of from the source
- Prepend the first edge's trunk to the new route
- Record branch points in `graph.trunkJunctions` for later T-junction drawing
- Skip groups involving self-referencing edges (their loop shapes shouldn't be modified)
- `AsciiGraph.trunkJunctions: GridCoord[]` field added to `types.ts`, initialized in `converter.ts`

#### 3. Box-border-aware connector placement

**Problem:** `drawBoxStart` places the junction character at `firstLine[0].x - 1`, derived from `gridToDrawingCoord` on the edge's start grid cell. When a sibling edge's `determineLabelLine` widens that column (to fit its label), the cell center shifts right, and the connector follows — even though the actual box border hasn't moved. The LR Top edge's `├` floats 2–3 chars right of the Source box.

**Fix (`draw.ts`):**
- `drawArrow`: computes `startPoint` via `getNodeAttachmentPoint` (actual box border), passes to `drawPath` and `drawBoxStart`
- `drawPath`: accepts optional `startPointOverride` for the first segment's start coordinate
- `drawBoxStart`: simplified — accepts `startDir` and `startPoint` directly, uses `startPoint` for character placement
- State-pseudo shape check moved inline into `drawArrow`

#### 4. Collinear corner skip + trunk-junction overlay

**Problem:** After trunk-sharing, the Right edge's path has a collinear intermediate point at the branch coordinate (e.g., `(5,1)` with Right→Right directions). `drawCorners` finds no matching corner case and outputs fallback `+`, overwriting the Center edge's `┐` at the same coordinate. Additionally, `drawLine` offsets leave a gap at the branch point.

**Fix (`draw.ts`):**
- `drawCorners` (and the two bundled-edge corner loops in `drawBundledEdgeSegment` and `drawBundleSharedPath`): skip intermediate points where `prevDir === nextDir` (collinear)
- `drawGraph`: after corners are merged, draw T-junction characters (`┬` for horizontal trunk, `├` for vertical trunk) at each `trunkJunction` coordinate from the post-processing

### Testing

- 4 new golden-file test cases added (ASCII + Unicode, TD + LR fan-out with edge labels)
- All 715 tests pass (711 original + 4 new)

### Files changed

| File | Δ |
|------|---|
| `src/ascii/pathfinder.ts` | `buildMoveDirs`, `getPath(preferredDir)`, `<=` in sinkDown |
| `src/ascii/edge-routing.ts` | Pass `preferredDir` to `getPath` |
| `src/ascii/draw.ts` | `startPointOverride` in `drawPath`, `getNodeAttachmentPoint` in `drawArrow`, collinear-skip in `drawCorners`, trunk-junction `┬`/`├` overlay |
| `src/ascii/grid.ts` | Trunk-sharing post-processing, self-reference guard |
| `src/ascii/types.ts` | `trunkJunctions: GridCoord[]` |
| `src/ascii/converter.ts` | Initialize `trunkJunctions: []` |
| `testdata/{ascii,unicode}/td_fanout_labels.txt` | New golden test (TD) |
| `testdata/{ascii,unicode}/lr_fanout_labels.txt` | New golden test (LR) |

Fixes #111
Fixes #112

title: Fix mergeEdges render option being ignored
author: dfadler
body:
## Summary

`layoutGraphSync` in `src/layout-engine.ts` merged the caller's `RenderOptions` with `DEFAULTS`, but then called `elkToPositioned(result, graph, DEFAULTS.mergeEdges)` — using the un-merged default instead of `opts.mergeEdges`. This meant `renderMermaidSVG(diagram, { mergeEdges: false })` silently had no effect; edge bundling was always applied regardless of what the caller passed.

Separately, `mergeEdges` was implemented end-to-end (`layout-engine/edge-bundling.ts`, `layout-engine/from-elk.ts`) but was never declared on the public `RenderOptions` type in `src/types.ts`, so TypeScript consumers couldn't discover or pass it without a cast.

## Changes

- `src/layout-engine.ts`: use `opts.mergeEdges` instead of `DEFAULTS.mergeEdges`.
- `src/types.ts`: add the missing `mergeEdges?: boolean` field to `RenderOptions` with a doc comment.
- `src/__tests__/integration.test.ts`: add a regression test asserting that `mergeEdges: true` vs `false` actually produces different output.

## Credit

Ports the fix from lukilabs/beautiful-mermaid#57 by @leslie555 ("feat: expose mergeEdges in RenderOptions for edge bundling control"). The upstream PR's diff didn't apply cleanly since this fork split `layout-engine.ts` into `src/layout-engine/*` by pipeline stage, so the fix was reimplemented against the current file layout; the underlying bug and fix are the same.

title: Fix ASCII edge-routing crashes and fan-in/fan-out layout bugs
author: dfadler
body:
## Summary

Fixes all five bugs from issue #64 in the ASCII renderer's custom edge-routing/root-detection engine (`src/ascii/grid.ts`, `pathfinder.ts`, `edge-bundling.ts`, `edge-routing.ts`, `draw-arrows.ts`): two hard crashes plus three layout-quality issues.

## Fixes

1. **Unbounded pathfinding blowup (crash)** — the A* pathfinder's iteration cap (added in #52) was per-call, not render-wide, so a dense graph with many edges could still exhaust the heap across many calls even though each individual call was bounded. Added a render-wide iteration budget shared across every `getPath` call, plus an unobstructed-direct-route shortcut that skips A* entirely for the common case.
2. **Order-dependent root misdetection (crash)** — root detection was a single forward pass over parsed nodes in Map-insertion order, misclassifying a node as a root when a `child → parent` edge appeared after a `parent → grandchild` edge. Replaced with a two-pass, order-independent algorithm, plus a fallback seed for graphs that are entirely a cycle (no true root exists) so layout still places every node instead of crashing.
3. **Fan-in grouping** — root nodes are now grouped by shared downstream target before grid placement, instead of being placed sequentially and interleaving with unrelated fan-in clusters.
4. **Sibling trunk sharing** — sibling edges from the same source now prefer an unobstructed direct route over an equal-length A* zigzag, so they share a straight trunk instead of one taking an unnecessary detour.
5. **Box-start connector drift** — the connector no longer drifts off the source node's border when a sibling edge's label widens a shared grid column.

Also updated the `preserve_order_of_definition` golden fixture: its old expected output was itself a product of the order-dependent root bug (treating node A as a root when only B has no real incoming edge) — the new output reflects correct root detection.

## Verification

- `pnpm test` — 863 tests pass
- `pnpm run lint`, `pnpm run format:check`, `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit`, `pnpm run build` all pass
- `pnpm changeset status --since origin/main` — patch bump registered

**Both crash repros verified end-to-end**, not just via the test suite — ran the exact repro code from the issue directly against `renderMermaidASCII`:

```
bug1 (dense fan-in) completed in 26 ms, output length 7197
bug2 (order-dependent root) completed in 4 ms, output length 2764
```

Both previously hung indefinitely (bug 1) or threw `Map maximum size exceeded` (bug 2) on `main`.

**Bug 4 (sibling trunk sharing) before/after** — a source node with three labeled sibling edges (`Src -->|left*| Left`, `|center*| Center`, `|right*| Right`), rendered against `main` and this branch:

Before (the third branch's trunk visibly bends through an unnecessary detour, riding along `center*`'s row before splitting off):
```
┌─────────────┐                                           
│             │                                           
│    Source   ├─────┬───────┐                             
│             │     │       │                             
└──────┬──────┘     └────center*──────────────────┐       
       │                    │                     │       
     left*                  │                  right*     
       │                    │                     │       
       │                    │                     │       
       ▼                    ▼                     ▼       
┌─────────────┐     ┌───────────────┐     ┌──────────────┐
│             │     │               │     │              │
│ Left Target │     │ Center Target │     │ Right Target │
│             │     │               │     │              │
└─────────────┘     └───────────────┘     └──────────────┘
```

After (clean three-way split, each branch descends straight down through its own label):
```
┌─────────────┐                                           
│             │                                           
│    Source   ├─────────────┬─────────────────────┐       
│             │             │                     │       
└──────┬──────┘          center*               right*     
       │                    │                     │       
     left*                  │                     │       
       │                    │                     │       
       │                    │                     │       
       ▼                    ▼                     ▼       
┌─────────────┐     ┌───────────────┐     ┌──────────────┐
│             │     │               │     │              │
│ Left Target │     │ Center Target │     │ Right Target │
│             │     │               │     │              │
└─────────────┘     └───────────────┘     └──────────────┘
```

(Bugs 3 and 5 were also fixed and covered by regression tests, but didn't produce a visually distinct before/after on the specific repros tried — bug 3's issue repro happened to already lay out identically for that particular node arrangement, and bug 5 (connector drift) is a subtler few-column shift that's clearer in the raw coordinate assertions than in a rendered diff.)

title: fix(ascii): give opposite-direction edge pairs distinct lanes (#629)
author: dfadler
body:
## Summary

Closes #629.

Two edges between the same pair of side-by-side nodes running in *opposite* directions reproduced #329's original defect byte for byte: both labels composited onto one line, one arrowhead dropped.

## Root cause

#329's `assignParallelEdgeLanes` keyed its grouping on the **ordered** pair `(source, target)`, so `Browser --> Server` and `Server --> Browser` landed in different groups and neither was tagged as a sibling of the other.

## Changes

- `parallelGroupKey` orders the two node names so a reciprocal pair shares one lane group — but only when laid out side by side on one row (`sharesHorizontalChannel`). A vertically-stacked pair is deliberately left alone: `drawTextOnLine` already de-collides that case (#530) via a mechanism that only works on a vertical segment; laning it would break #530.
- `determinePath` swaps in the alternative start/end direction pair for a lane edge whose preferred pair is degenerate (same face at both ends). `buildParallelLanePath` reads that shape as a vertical departure and offsets along the wrong axis otherwise. Forward edges are unaffected (their preferred/alternative pairs are identical).
- `canBundle` refuses to fold a lane-assigned edge into a fan-in/fan-out trunk — defensive, currently unreachable, marked as such.

## Verification

Every existing ASCII sample renders byte-identically (diffed `renderMermaidASCII` over all of `samples-data.ts`) — the Playwright baselines are untouched. Sabotage-tested both halves of the fix.

## Test plan

- [x] `ascii-reverse-direction-edges-629.test.ts` (13 tests) covers the issue's full trigger table
- [x] Full suite green; lint, format, typecheck, build clean; diff coverage 100%
- [x] **Real-terminal before/after screenshots via `verify-ascii-terminal`** — see [Visual verification](#visual-verification) below

## Visual verification

```mermaid
  Browser -- request --> Server
  Server -- response --> Browser
```

title: fix(flowchart): break edges over subgraph title text with a mask (#1239, part 1)
author: dfadler
body:
Partial fix for #1239 (does not close it): the "edges cross subgraph titles" half only.

## What changed

An edge that comes down over the top of a subgraph to reach a node inside could land on the subgraph's title text. mermaid.js draws these edges through the text too, so this does not reroute anything. The edge is not painted over the text itself, and carries on past it.

It is done with an SVG `<mask>` (`packages/svg-renderer/src/title-gaps.ts`, used from `renderer.ts`): a hole the size of the title text, plus 2px of padding. The edge stays one `<polyline>`/`<path>` with the same points and `data-*` attributes, so nothing that selects or counts edges changes.

- The mask is only emitted when an edge actually crosses a title, and only that edge gets the `mask` attribute. A diagram with no such edge is byte-identical.
- `maskUnits="userSpaceOnUse"` is needed: with the default bounding-box units a straight vertical edge has a zero-width box and the whole edge would be masked away.
- The mask id is derived from the hole positions, so two inline diagrams on one page never share an id with different content.

This replaces an earlier version of this PR that moved the edge sideways, or detoured it down the outer wall (`routeEdgesAroundGroupTitles`). That drifted from how mermaid draws these edges and left the edge hugging the subgraph border. It is removed.

title: fix(flowchart): land an edge on a diamond's vertex, not its slope (#1239, part 4)
author: dfadler
body:
Partial fix for #1239 (does not close it): an edge that meets a decision diamond straight on lands on its vertex instead of its slope. **Stacked on #1311** (which is stacked on #1309); the base is #1311's branch, so the diff is only this change. Retarget to `main` once those merge.

## What changed

ELK treats a diamond as a rectangle and aims an incoming edge at a port on the bounding box's face, usually off the face's centre. Shape clipping then drops that off-centre line onto the diamond's slanted side, so the arrowhead lands on the slope. mermaid.js aims every edge at the node's centre, so an edge that arrives straight on lands on the vertex. In the CI/CD sample, "Deploy Staging" into "QA Approved?" ended on the upper-left slope, 27px off the top vertex.

New pass `snapEdgesToDiamondVertices` (`packages/svg-renderer/src/layout-engine/diamond-vertex-snap.ts`, called from `from-elk.ts` just before shape clipping) moves the edge's last bend and final run onto the face's centre line. The run before that bend is a jog, so it just gets longer or shorter. Clipping then lands the edge on the vertex.

It is deliberately conservative. An edge is left as ELK drew it when:

- it is not an incoming edge to a diamond that arrives straight on, or it is already on the centre line;
- it has no perpendicular jog to shorten (a straight run, or three points in line), since moving it would mean moving its source;
- several edges share that face of the diamond, or an edge leaves from it, so ELK's spread is kept;
- the moved route would pass within 2px of another node;
- the final run would be under 10px, too short for the arrowhead.

Outgoing ends are never touched. The two edges that fork out of a decision leave from both lower slopes in mermaid too, so those already match.

## Blast radius

Of the 30 diamond ends across all 97 samples in `samples-data.ts`, exactly one incoming end is off-centre: this one. Hashing SVG and ASCII output for every sample with and without the pass: only **CI/CD Pipeline** changes. ASCII output is unchanged.

## Not addressed

The edge still has a jog before the vertex, because "Deploy Staging" and "QA Approved?" are not in one column (mermaid.js puts them in one). That is ELK's node placement, not edge clipping. I tried `bk.fixedAlignment` NONE, LEFTDOWN and RIGHTDOWN, and `nodePlacement.strategy` NETWORK_SIMPLEX and LINEAR_SEGMENTS: none aligns them, and `NONE`, the best for bend count, changes 40 of 97 SVG samples. That needs its own investigation. The git branching trunk (the other half of #1239) is also untouched.

title: fix(flowchart): break cycles the way mermaid does so a cyclic flowchart isn't inverted (#1239, part 5)
author: dfadler
body:
Partial fix for #1239 (does not close it): the inverted flow in the Git Branching sample. Independent of #1309, #1311 and #1312; based on `main`.

## What changed

ELK breaks the cycles in a flowchart with its own heuristic, and it can reverse the wrong edge of a cycle and draw the whole diagram upside down. In the Git Branching sample, `Tests?` was the leftmost node and `main` sat in the middle, so the flow read backwards: `Tests? -> main -> develop -> ...` instead of starting at `main`.

mermaid.js breaks cycles with a depth-first walk (dagre's acyclic step): starting from each node in order and following out-edges in source order, an edge that points at a node still on the walk's stack is reversed. Which edge of a cycle gets reversed decides the whole layout. This PR does the same:

- `findBackEdgeIndexes` (`packages/svg-renderer/src/layout-engine/back-edges.ts`) finds those edges with an iterative depth-first walk (so a long chain can't overflow the stack).
- `mermaidToElk` hands ELK those edges already reversed, so ELK sees an acyclic graph and never has a cycle to break.
- `elkToPositioned` flips each reversed edge's points back, so it still runs from its source to its target (arrowheads, labels and `data-*` attributes are unchanged).

Flowcharts only. State diagrams have their own cycle breaking, and a graph with a subgraph direction override goes through hop edges and ports this does not rewrite, so both are left as they were (`edgesReversedForLayout` returns an empty set for them).

## Blast radius

Hashed SVG and ASCII output for all 97 samples in `samples-data.ts` with and without the change: only **Git Branching Workflow** changes. ASCII output is unchanged.

## Not addressed

- CI/CD Pipeline is **not** changed by this, although it has the same kind of cycle. ELK lays a subgraph's contents out as a block before the nodes around it, so an edge from outside cannot pull `Fix & Retry` further down, whichever edge is reversed. Matching mermaid.js there needs a different approach to subgraph layout and is tracked separately.
- In Git Branching, the `pass` edge from `Tests?` back to `main` still takes a long route around the diagram, as a long back edge does in mermaid.js. And the edges sharing one vertical trunk next to `develop` (the other half of #1239) are untouched.

## Visual verification (browser-rendered SVG)

Two examples, one per flow direction. In each, "before" is this branch with the pre-reversal turned off (`main` behavior) and "after" is this PR.

### Horizontal (`graph LR`): Git Branching sample

```mermaid
  C --> E{PR Review}
  D --> E
  E -->|approved| B

  F --> G{Tests?}
  G -->|pass| A
  G -->|fail| F
```

Before (top) and after (bottom). The flow now starts at `main` and reads `main -> develop -> feature/* -> PR Review`, `release/1.0 -> Tests?`, left to right as mermaid.js draws it.

![horizontal](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/af25cc09-97cd-4cd4-96c8-0ee958aed1b3)

### Vertical (`graph TD`): CI-style cycle with a dotted back edge

```mermaid
  B -->|No| D[Fix & Retry]
  D -.-> A
  C --> E([Deploy Staging])
  E --> F{QA Approved?}
  F -->|Yes| G((Production))
  F -->|No| D
```

Before (left) and after (right). Before, the diagram is upside down: `Push Code` sits at the bottom and `Tests Pass?` at the top. After, it flows top to bottom from `Push Code`, and the `Fix & Retry -> Push Code` edge runs up the side into the bottom of `Push Code`.

![vertical](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0aa2f330-d72b-4950-87f4-5b2922d53256)

## Tests

`src/__tests__/flowchart-back-edge-prereversal-1239.test.ts`:

- `findBackEdgeIndexes`: nothing in an acyclic graph; a simple cycle and a two-node cycle; node order decides where the walk starts; `D -.-> A` and not `F --> D` in the CI/CD cycle; a cross edge to a finished node is not a back edge; self-loops are ignored; a 20,000-node cycle doesn't overflow the stack.

title: feat(flowchart): lay out subgraphs the way mermaid.js does (#1239, part 6)
author: dfadler
body:
Partial fix for #1239 (does not close it): lays out flowcharts with subgraphs the way mermaid.js arranges them. Supersedes the CI/CD layout fix in #1309 and the routing fixes in #1311 (both closed; they assumed the old layout, see "What this replaces"). Builds on #1313 (cycle breaking) and #1314 (the layout oracle), both merged.

## The problem

ELK lays a subgraph's contents out as a block before the nodes around it. So a node outside a subgraph can never sit beside one deep inside it, and an edge from outside can't pull a member to a later layer. mermaid.js (dagre) lays the whole graph out flat, ranks every node on its own, and draws each subgraph as a box around its members, with the nodes that don't belong to it beside the box. In the CI/CD sample, official Mermaid puts `Deploy Staging`, `QA Approved?` and `Production` in a column to the left of the pipeline's box, and `Fix & Retry` at the bottom of the box. Ours stacked the box above them.

This is measured, not eyeballed. `pnpm run layout:oracle` (#1314) scores our layout against official mermaid.js as the share of node pairs placed in the same relation (above/below and left/right, within 20px). It now scores `layoutFlowchartSync`, the layout flowcharts use.

| Sample | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CI/CD Pipeline | 48% / 52% | **95% / 76%** |
| System Architecture | 82% / 93% | **96% / 93%** |
| Subgraphs | 100% / 100% | 100% / 100% |
| Nested Subgraphs | 100% / 100% | 100% / 100% |

CI/CD's 76% left/right is five of 21 pairs. mermaid.js fans `Push Code`, `Tests Pass?` and `Build Image` out to the right and left of each other (more than 20px apart), and puts `Production` under `Deploy Staging` and `QA Approved?`; ours keeps the first three in one column and `Production` 26px off the other two. Matching the fan would mean keeping the edge from `Tests Pass?` to `Fix & Retry` in the layout, where it goes round the outside of the box and makes the box more than twice as wide (see "Edges inside a box").

Subgraph diagrams in general had more room to improve than the samples show. Eight typical shapes (cluster in the middle, outsiders on both sides, a nested cluster with an outside edge, LR, BT, a loop through a cluster, ...), scored the same way (above/below, left/right; containment is 100% throughout). The sources are in `src/__tests__/compound-flat-layout.test.ts`:

| Diagram | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| outsiders on both sides | 100% / 27% | **100% / 100%** |
| LR cluster with outsiders | 27% / 93% | **100% / 100%** |
| two clusters, cross edges | 60% / 60% | **100% / 80%** |
| three clusters side by side | 47% / 40% | **67% / 93%** |
| the other four | 100% / 100% | 100% / 100% |

## What changed

New `layoutFlowchartSync` (`packages/svg-renderer/src/layout-engine.ts`), used by the flowchart module in the registry. `layoutGraphSync` is unchanged and still used by architecture diagrams, which share the engine. The algorithm is in `layout-engine/compound-flat.ts`:

1. **Lay the graph out flat** (no subgraphs) to learn the layers and each node's position across the flow. Layers are found by overlap along the flow axis, not by centre, because ELK left-aligns the nodes of an LR layer.
2. **Spine nodes.** In a layer between a subgraph's first and last member where it has no member, add an invisible *spine* node, chained to the subgraph's members in the layers either side. It stands for the box in that layer, so ELK keeps the layer's other nodes out of the box's way. It starts narrow and is widened only as far as needed (a secant estimate from the last two runs).
3. **Order.** The nodes are given to ELK left to right so each subgraph's members stay together: from where the first layout put them, with every outsider inside a subgraph's layers on the side of it its connections already chose. Sibling subgraphs side by side are put in mermaid.js's order, the reverse of declaration (#444), unless edges run both ways between them, in which case they keep the order the layout gave them (that is what mermaid.js does for the "two clusters, cross edges" shape).
4. **Lay out again, then draw the boxes** (nested, using the same padding as before, `SUBGRAPH_PADDING`) around the real members. The spine nodes and their edges are dropped from the result.
5. **Open room between boxes only where they meet.** A box is kept 40px from what is around it (`BOX_CLEARANCE`; mermaid.js leaves 40 to 50px). Where two boxes, or a box and a node, are closer than that, everything past the first of them is moved along by the shortfall, and the edges' points with it, so just that gap grows. (An earlier version widened the spacing between every layer, which stretched the gaps inside boxes to about twice what `main` has.) A node that straddles the cut stays put, and an edge's bends in the gap stay beside the first box, so the bus out of `Load Balancer` stays above the region titles.

### Edges inside a box

An edge between two members that spans a layer where the subgraph has only a spine node has to get past the spine, and ELK sends it round the outside, which drags its end node, and so the box, sideways. In CI/CD that was `Tests Pass?` to `Fix & Retry` and the dotted edge back to `Push Code`: the box was 449px wide, and the canvas 835px. These edges are now left out of the layout (`LayoutHints.detachedEdges`) and drawn afterwards through the box by `layout-engine/inner-edges.ts`: the cheapest route (length plus a cost per bend) that stays inside the box, clear of every node and at least 14px from the other inside edges. A decision's branch leaves by its side, as mermaid.js draws it; a back edge hooks up the side of the box and into the target's side. The box is 211px wide and the canvas 481px. If an inside edge has no clear route, the layout is done again with the edges left in.

### Plumbing

All optional and inert without hints, in `to-elk.ts` and `layout-hints.ts`: `LayoutHints` carries fixed node widths, edges that must not be straightened (spine edges, via `elk.layered.priority.straightness`), edges to leave out (above), a separate walk order for #1313's back-edge search (the node order is also the order ELK is given the nodes in), and forced node order within layers.

**Falls back to the old layout** (`layoutGraphSync`) when the new one doesn't apply or can't be made to fit: a subgraph with its own direction (laid out as its own graph), state diagrams, an edge to a subgraph (the parser gives it a node with the subgraph's id), a subgraph with no node, a node id that collides with a spine id, or boxes that still cover a node after the retries. So it can't produce a worse-than-before overlap.

## What this replaces

- **#1309** (subgraphs first in ELK's node order) fixed the inversion but, measured by the oracle, left CI/CD at 81% / 5%: it turned the diagram the right way up while stacking the subgraph above the chain where mermaid draws them side by side. This PR gets the arrangement itself right. Closed.
- **#1311** (back-edge routing and the diamond-vertex snap) was written for #1309's layout, where `Fix & Retry` sits early and `QA Approved? -> Fix & Retry` is a long back edge. Here `Fix & Retry` ranks after `QA Approved?`, so that edge is forward and there is no loop to fix. Closed; #1312 (diamond vertex landing) merged separately.

## Cost

Median of 40 runs per diagram on this machine (Node 22), `layoutGraphSync` against `layoutFlowchartSync`: Subgraphs 3.4 to 2.9 ms, Nested Subgraphs 3.3 to 3.2 ms, CI/CD 4.2 to 8.3 ms, System Architecture 4.2 to 4.2 ms. title: Flowchart layout: orient subgraph feedback edges like mermaid 12's ELK (#1993)
author: dfadler
body:
Closes #1993

## What

Mermaid 12's ELK layout reverses the edge that closes a cycle between a subgraph and the nodes around it before ELK breaks any other cycle (`orientFeedbackEdges`, `findSubgraphFeedbackEdges` in mermaid's `elk/subgraphFeedbackEdges.ts`; the default preset then uses `cycleBreaking.strategy = DEPTH_FIRST`, `considerModelOrder = NODES_AND_EDGES`, `INCLUDE_CHILDREN`; read in `mermaid@12.1.0`'s `chunks/mermaid.core/elk-*.mjs`). We reversed a flat depth-first back edge instead, which in CI/CD picked `D -.-> A` and put `Fix & Retry` under `QA Approved?`.

This adds `subgraphFeedbackEdges` (back-edges.ts), a port of that lifted-edge walk, and reverses its edges first; the existing depth-first walk then runs on the rest. The compound layout hands the set to its flat passes through a new `LayoutHints.feedbackEdges` (they have no subgraphs of their own). No ELK option changed, no new layout engine.

## Design: what was tried first (oracle vs mermaid 12.1.0, worst figure per sample, all flowchart samples)

| Candidate | CI/CD | Others |
| --- | --- | --- |
| main | 48 | - |
| subgraph feedback + flat DFS (this PR) | **90** | none moved |
| subgraph feedback + ELK `DEPTH_FIRST` | 90 | none moved |
| subgraph feedback + ELK `GREEDY_MODEL_ORDER` | 90 | Git Branching 100 -> 71 |
| subgraph feedback + ELK `MODEL_ORDER` | 24 | 8 samples drop |
| no pre-reversal + ELK `DEPTH_FIRST` | 48 | CJK Labels 50 -> 17 |
| no pre-reversal + `GREEDY_MODEL_ORDER` | 52 | Git Branching 71 |

title: fix(ascii): ER junctions at crossings, labels on their own edge, no edge along a box border (#2112)
author: dfadler
body:
Closes #2112

## What changed

ER ASCII/Unicode vertical edges (`packages/ascii-renderer/src/er-diagram.ts`; `edge-routing.ts`, `grid.ts` and `port-offsets.ts` are untouched):

- **Junctions at crossings.** `setCGuarded` draws `┼` (`+` in the ASCII charset) where a horizontal and a vertical line meet, instead of the later write erasing the earlier line. An existing junction is never overwritten.
- **No edge along a box border.** Jog rows start past the tallest cardinality marker, each edge takes its own free row (a stem may cross another edge's jog but two horizontal runs never share a row), and bypass jogs search their own free row in the gap instead of sitting directly under the box. The row gap grows by one row per edge crossing it, plus two per same-row detour; rows widen when a vertical edge has a label.
- **Labels on their own edge.** Vertical-edge labels are placed after all lines are drawn (a mid-loop label could cover a stem a later edge took). A one-line label goes on its own horizontal run with a blank each side when the run is long enough (like mermaid's label on the path); otherwise beside its own stem (upper or lower), preferring rows in a gap, clear of other edges' lines and markers. A jog toward the left takes the lowest free row and toward the right the highest, which keeps the corridor beside a stem open for its label.

- The issue's graph (gallery 157/158) no longer has the closed rectangle on current `origin/main`: #2121 (flow-face lanes) and #2109 removed it, and `CROSSINGS` in `ascii-duplicate-edges-2025-2028-2030.test.ts` is already `{}`. - What is still there is the seeded ratchet (15 over 48 graphs) and, over 600 seeds, 207 closed rectangles. Classified from the real edge paths:
  - **Avoidable, ordering**: lanes only grow outward, but they were routed in edge order, so a long lane or long plain edge took an inner track and every shorter lane nested inside it crossed it (seed 1: `n2 --> n0` over two lane groups; LR seed 114: the duplicate `n2 --> n0` lanes inside the `n0/n1` and `n1/n2` lanes).

title: fix(ascii): lay out and route a decision's opposing pair like mermaid, without crossing (#2492)
author: dfadler
body:
Refs #2492

Opposing edges (`B -->|no| D` + `D --> B`) in LR drew one merged route when B is a diamond or D a parallelogram, and the nodes were not laid out as mermaid lays them out. `port-offsets.ts` only splits a shared port where the border glyph is a plain `─`/`│`; a diamond's bottom vertex (`╲╱`) and a parallelogram's slanted side (`╱`/`╲`) were rejected, so both strokes stayed on the same cells.

## What changed

1. **Split at the vertex / slanted side.** Both glyph kinds are accepted as places to draw a second stroke (slanted sides only for parallelograms, scanning inward past blanks).
2. **Lay the nodes out like mermaid.** In the GitHub render of this source, `Read Input` and `Valid?` share a row, `Write Output` is above and `Ask Again` below, so the decision is centred between its branches. `centerParentsOverChildren` (`grid.ts`) already does that, but it switched off for the whole graph as soon as any edge pointed backwards, and `D --> B` does. For a diamond, the reverse of a forward edge one rank down is now treated as the other half of a reciprocal pair, and it no longer counts as a "second parent" that stops the parent moving with it. Plain boxes keep the old layout (an existing test pins it).
3. **Route like mermaid.** `no` leaves the diamond's right corner and drops into Ask Again's left side; the return leaves below it, runs under `no` and enters the diamond's lower-right face, so they never cross and nothing uses the bottom vertex.
   - `grid.ts`: an LR diamond with a reciprocal pair (and no self-loop) is marked `fanOutCentered`, so its branches leave the right face (the #2351/#2366 convention).
   - `edge-routing.ts`: the back edge into such a diamond heads for the right face and its L route is drawn directly (the search otherwise floods under the diamond's own block and hits the A* cap). Later parallel returns (`parallelLane.index > 0`) keep their own lanes.
   - `port-offsets.ts`: `nestedRow` gives the edge with the farther-left lane the lower rows at both nodes; `nestedPush` keeps two same-way L edges nested at a vertical port face.
   - `canvas.ts`: the RL flip swapped glyphs at a diamond's rect edge cells as if they were box corners, leaving a stray `│`; it now swaps only border cells.

## Summary

Refs #2913. Closes #3156. The topology gate's last four edge-end face misses (804/808) were all one construct: self-loops on a member of a frame with its own `direction` (the fork-fixes entry `ascii-subgraph-self-loops-frame-direction`). The gate is now **808/808**.

**Cause.** mermaid@12.3.0 draws a self-loop by the direction its node is laid out in: the innermost frame whose own `direction` applies, else the diagram's (left face for TD/BT, top face for LR/RL). Our SVG layout used the diagram's direction, so a `direction LR` frame in a TD diagram drew its loops on the left, squeezed into the gap beside the previous node (see the SVG screenshots). ELK's hints for ASCII said L while mermaid, and the grid, draw them over the top. #3114 hid that mismatch in ASCII with an L/T rotation.

**Fix.**
- `packages/svg-renderer/src/layout-engine/from-elk.ts`: `synthesizeSelfLoopEdges` takes a per-node effective direction (`subgraphDirectionIsHonored`, the same rule `subgraphToElk` uses). `simple-layout.ts` keeps the diagram's direction, since it ignores frame directions.
- `packages/ascii-renderer/src/grid.ts`: drop #3114's rotation, take a frame's loop hints without the root's mirror, and reverse the ends only where the root flips along the frame's axis (RL root for LR/RL frames, BT root for TD/BT frames).
- `packages/ascii-renderer/src/flowchart.ts` + `converter.ts`: a frame with its own direction is oriented by it alone, on both axes. mermaid@12.3.0 puts a frame’s nodes, title and edges in the same places under every root (measured for a fan-out in all 16 root x frame pairs), but a `BT` root still mirrored the cross axis of an `LR`/`RL` frame (`b` above `c` came out below, and these loops below the node) and an `RL` root that of a `TD`/`BT` frame. `flipSubgraphRegions` now flips both axes back and `titleBelow` follows the frame’s own direction.

title: ASCII gate: read a decision's TD/BT slant start off the drawn cell (Refs #3161)

## Summary

Refs #3161 (not closed). The ASCII topology gate (`scripts/lib/ascii-topology.ts`) maps a decision's start to a face from the drawn first stroke cell for LR/RL only (`diamondStartDir`, PR #3039 cause C). This extends the same reading to TD/BT: a start left of the diamond's middle column is on its lower-left slant (B/L, T/L in BT), right of it the lower-right slant, on it the vertex (B, T in BT). **The gate's measurement changed, the drawing did not** (`packages/ascii-renderer/**` is untouched). A start on the vertex still reads as the flow face, so the mapping can only add faces that `ADJ` already accepts; it never loosens a passing end.

Parity target mermaid@12.3.0 (headless, default layout, via `scripts/lib/real-mermaid.ts`; `node_modules/mermaid` is 12.3.0). Not checked on GitHub (12.2.0) or mermaid.live.

### Gate before/after (`--misses`, 105 samples, all exact)

| run | edge-end faces before | after | end cells | arrowheads |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| default | 814/816 | **815/816** | 387/387 | 404/404 |
| `--dir TD` | 810/816 | **812/816** | 375/378 | 401/404 |
| `--dir LR` | 813/816 | 813/816 | 396/399 | 401/404 |
| `--dir RL` | 811/816 | 811/816 | 396/399 | 401/404 |
| `--dir BT` | 806/816 | **808/816** | 375/378 | 401/404 |

Layer, order, alignment, self-loop and subgraph lines are identical before and after. End cells and arrowheads did not move (they were not in scope).

After merging a later `origin/main` (6 more edge ends from new samples, all passing) the same runs read default 821/822, TD 818/822, BT 814/822; the misses are unchanged.

**This is 815, not the 816 the brief hoped for, and TD/BT gain +2, not +4/+6.** The drawing does not leave on the slant for two of the four ends the triage expected to move, so they stay counted as misses.

### Per end (drawn first stroke cell vs diamond middle column; ELK hint order; mermaid@12.3.0 start offset from the diamond centre, half-extent 87)

`ENTRY ascii-parallel-lanes-hint-order` (TD and BT):

| end | ELK | drawn first cell (x, mid x=9) | mermaid@12.3.0 | now |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `n3->n2` VW (#0) | L | 9: the vertex | (-46, 41): lower-left slant | **still a miss**: the grid draws VW at the vertex and `38` under the left slant, mermaid and ELK have VW outermost on the slant (the "opposite order" caveat on that fork-fixes entry) |

`Decision Self-Loop with Duplicate Edges` (TD and BT):

| end | ELK | drawn first cell (x, mid x=16) | mermaid@12.3.0 | now |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `n0->n2` #1 | L | 15: under the lower-left slant | (-51, 36): lower-left slant | **fixed**: reads B/L |
| `n0->n2` #2 | B | 14 | (-26, 61) | passes |
| `n0->n1` #3 | B | 17 | (0, 87): the vertex | passes |
| `n0->n1` #5 | R | 16: the vertex | (51, 36): lower-right slant | **still a miss**: drawn at the vertex, mermaid and ELK leave on the right slant (grid and mermaid have #3 and #5 in the opposite order) |

title: ASCII: a duplicate pair plus a reciprocal draws three straight strokes in TD/BT
author: dfadler
body:
Stacked on #3205 (cause B). Its head branch, and #3201's, are merged into this one so the gate is measured against their routing, so the diff against `main` also holds their changes; this PR is based on #3205's branch and retargets to `main` once that merges. Cause C of the forced-direction misses in the ASCII topology gate.

## Summary

A duplicate pair plus a reciprocal between two stacked nodes (`n1 --> n0`, `n0 --> n1`, `n1 --> n0`) under `flowchart TD` or `BT` drew the second duplicate round the side faces (R/R). mermaid@12.3.0 draws three straight vertical strokes, in declaration order, on the facing faces, and so does ELK.

**Cause** (traced with logging, not read off the drawing): `spreadsOnFaces` (`edge-routing.ts`) refuses the `n1->n0` x2 group because its "nothing else may use the facing faces" loop counts the reciprocal `n0->n1` as another user of those faces. The group falls to lanes and `routeAsLane` sends the second duplicate to the side faces. The `twin` and reciprocal gates in `determinePath` are not involved.

**Fix:** a single unlabeled reciprocal joins an unlabeled duplicate pair in one column (`reciprocalStrokes`), and `spreadParallelEdges` (`port-offsets.ts`) groups the pair and its reciprocal by port pair, on vertical strokes only. A plain reciprocal pair, labeled groups and horizontal flows keep their routing.

title: ASCII: LR/RL cluster-exit sibling fans go round the target, as mermaid@12.3.0 routes them
author: dfadler
body:
## Summary

Part of the cluster-exit sibling group of [#2886](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/issues/2886) (left-to-right and right-to-left only; this PR does not close it).

Three or more edges that leave one subgraph for one target now go round the target in LR and RL ASCII output, the way mermaid@12.3.0 routes them: the first siblings rise beside the cluster, run over the target and drop beside it, the last ones dip under it the same way, the middle one stays straight, and the routes nest so none cross. TD and BT are unchanged.

What changed:

- `packages/ascii-renderer/src/cluster-fans.ts` (new): finds the fans from the ELK hint (a bend of 0.55 or more beside the target), grows the grid with the rows and columns they run on (an over track, an under track, a rise column, a drop column and a spare column between them for labels), and builds each as a six-point route. `port-offsets.ts` spreads the nested runs onto rows and columns of their own, and `edge-routing.ts` routes and labels them.
- The cluster's exits sit two rows apart and the target's entries one apart. mermaid@12.3.0's ports are about 15px apart on the cluster and 5px on the target, so its drop into the target is the longer leg; at one row each the two legs tied and the strict bend read the wrong one. `hintedFaceCells` makes the cluster face tall enough and `placeFace` keeps the entries one apart.
- New layout-only option `layoutEdgeLabelFontSize` in `packages/svg-renderer`: mermaid boxes edge labels at 16px, the SVG draws them at 11px. With it set, the `edgeEdge: 70` that stood in for the boxes is not used (12 instead). Off by default, so SVG output and every other graph's hints are unchanged. The ASCII provider turns it on, with the mermaid node sizes, only for LR/RL graphs that have such a fan (`hasClusterFan`); using it for every subgraph graph broke 31 existing snapshots.
- `planJogRows` used the cluster's `maxY` as its wall on the LR axis, where it should be `maxX`.

## What was compared, and against what

Everything below is against **mermaid@12.3.0** (the pinned `mermaid`, headless Chromium, `scripts/lib/oracle-layout.ts`), strict tie rule: a real bend within 0.05 of 0.5 needs a drawn bend within 0.05 of 0.5, otherwise the same side.

| Strict bend sides vs mermaid@12.3.0 | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| LR | 140 / 162 | 147 / 162 |
| RL | 139 / 162 | 146 / 162 |
| TD | 163 / 188 | 163 / 188 |
| BT | 166 / 188 | 166 / 188 |

No edge moved to the wrong side in any direction. The edges that went right: `Five` #1 and #2 (real 0.90 and 0.80, drawn 0.86 and 0.77), `Six` #1 to #4 (real 0.91, 0.82, 0.73, 0.37; drawn 0.88, 0.81, 0.73, 0.35) and `Nine` #1 and #2 (real 0.93, 0.86; drawn 0.90, 0.83).

`pnpm exec tsx scripts/ascii-topology.ts --dir LR|RL|TD|BT`: layer pairs, in-layer order pairs, edge-end faces, end cells and arrowheads are unchanged in all four directions. The gate's own `bend sides` (scored against our ELK hint, not mermaid) goes LR 175 to 177 and RL 174 to 176; I am not counting that as progress. Alignment pairs are the same count (569/905 LR and RL) with mean deviation 0.70 to 0.71.

Every changed drawing was compared with mermaid@12.3.0. All 260 sample-by-direction renders were diffed before and after: only the LR and RL renders of `Five`, `Six`, `Nine Cluster Exit Siblings` and `Cluster Exit Siblings with No Other Exit` changed (8 renders). Their bends are in the table above and `No Other Exit` is real 0.77 / 0.77, drawn 0.80 / 0.80. No new crossings: the routes nest (first sibling outermost on both ends) and `other` drops in the leftmost rise column.

Labelled and dense cases (the trap in #3227): the fans are labelled in all four samples; I also checked wide labels and an extra node in the gutter (`first label`, `second`, an unlabelled edge, `fourth`, `fifth one`, `other`, and `X --> T`). Labels sit on the over or under run, arrowheads stay one per sibling, nothing is lost. That case still differs from mermaid in one place, filed as #3238.

On GitHub-rendered mermaid or mermaid.live (Playwright, mermaid.live `view` page, whatever mermaid version it serves, not necessarily 12.3.0): `Five` and `Nine` LR draw the same nested shape (screenshots below). That shows the topology, which siblings go over and which under, and where `other` drops. It does not show the pinned version's numbers, and a browser draws curves at pixel scale, so it says nothing about bend fractions.

## Tests

- `__tests__/ascii-cluster-fan-2886.test.ts`: `Five`, `Six`, `Nine` and `No Other Exit`, LR and RL. Arrowhead counts, the first sibling's run above T and the last below it, the outer siblings' bends 0.55 or more and nested, and an SVG and an ASCII snapshot per case (allow-listed in `scripts/check-snapshot-allowlist.sh`).
- `packages/svg-renderer/src/__tests__/layout-edge-label-boxes.test.ts`: with the option, `Five Cluster Exit Siblings` (TD) lays out within 6px of mermaid@12.3.0's 196 / -25 / 192; without it the default layout is untouched.
- Sabotage checks, each making the new tests fail (24, 16 and 16 of 24): the fan planner off, the two-row exit spacing off, the entries allowed two rows apart.
- `pnpm run verify` and `pnpm run verify --ci-gates` pass; `pnpm exec playwright test -g ascii-samples` has the same two failures on this branch and on `main` (`Interactivity: Step Routing`, `Dense Duplicate Edges (TD)`, darwin baselines), none from this change. `check-diff-coverage` reports no instrumented lines changed.
- Existing suite: 15060 tests pass with the existing snapshots untouched.

## Still open, with the real limit

- TD and BT cluster-exit siblings: real mermaid@12.3.0 draws near-straight drops with one shared bend row (0.68); the grid needs a row per sibling. #3233.
- The gate's `bend sides` reads a U route's rise where mermaid's longest run is the drop. #3234.
- The SVG layout's edge-label boxes (11px, with the `edgeEdge: 70` stand-in) are still not mermaid's 16px by default. #3235.
- Wide labels rank the outer siblings' legs the other way from mermaid in one case, and `Five` #3 is a straight stroke where mermaid draws a 7px dogleg, under the half cell the grid can show. #3238.
- A property-test seed that fails on `main` as well, found along the way. #3239.
